summary: Reconciliation is well-defined and sorry-free but larger than the four named duplicates. HasAnd/HasOr/HasImp/HasBox are field-for-field identical between the fork's Connectives.lean and upstream's Operators.lean (same class name, namespace, field name, projection type), so adopting upstream's and deleting the fork's requires ZERO call-site edits across all 1,802 references. HasDia -> HasDiamond is a 6-code-site rename (17 lines counting docs). The fork-only classes (HasBot, HasUntil, HasSince, HasNext) and all six bundles collide with nothing and are kept as the upstreamable delta. The load-bearing finding, measured empirically for the first time here, is a SECOND-ORDER notation collision: upstream's Operators.lean attaches scoped notation for the same symbols to the typeclass projections in namespace Cslib.Logic, which is an ENCLOSING namespace of the fork's Cslib.Logic.{PL,Modal,Bimodal,Temporal,LTL}, so both interpretations go live and Lean raises a hard 'Ambiguous term' error. Exactly 12 collision sites across 5 files were enumerated by simulating the full upstream notation set against all five formula types; everything else in the fork's notation is provably safe because the corresponding instance is absent (sole surviving interpretation resolves silently). Separately: upstream commit b8ad3923 is NOT an ancestor of local HEAD and Operators.lean does not exist locally, so the task's 'verify with lake build' criterion forces phase 1 to be a verbatim vendoring of upstream's Operators.lean (unchanged since #607 merged; git merge-tree confirms it is a conflict-free add).

Keep unchanged. The neg/top Lukasiewicz defaulted fields on PropositionalConnectives are delegated to by all four concrete formula types, so dismantling the bundles is not a safe unilateral move.

NOTATION COLLISION (12 sites, 5 files), measured: Propositional/Defs.lean:107 (and) 108 (or) 109 (imp); Modal/Basic.lean:232 (and) 233 (or) 234 (imp) 235 (box) 236 (diamond); Bimodal/Syntax/Formula.lean:101 (imp) 102 (box); Temporal/Syntax/Formula.lean:169 (imp); LTL/Syntax/Formula.lean:209 (imp).

CONFIRMED CLEAN and must be left alone: the negation and biconditional notations in all five namespaces (no HasNot/HasIff instances anywhere in the fork), Bimodal/Temporal/LTL conjunction and disjunction, Bimodal and LTL diamond, LTL box (LTL binds box/diamond to allFuture/someFuture -- a different meaning that must be preserved), CLL tensor, and all temporal operator notations. Verified: when only one interpretation elaborates, Lean resolves silently with no error.

LATENT TRAP: those rows are clean only because an instance is missing. Registering HasNot, HasIff, HasAnd, HasOr, HasDiamond, or HasTensor for those types in any later task silently reopens the collision. Record as a standing invariant in the Connectives.lean module docstring.

recommended_phase_shape: Phase 1: vendor Operators.lean verbatim via `git show b8ad3923:Cslib/Foundations/Logic/Operators.lean`, add to Cslib.lean via `lake exe mk_all --module`. Never hand-edit the vendored file.

Phase 2: reduce Connectives.lean to a delta -- delete the four duplicates, add `public import Cslib.Foundations.Logic.Operators`, rename HasDia -> HasDiamond, relocate the HasBox design docstring (cited ChagrovZakharyaschev1997/Blackburn2001 material) into the module docstring, keep everything else.
Phase 3: propagate the rename across Axioms.lean, ProofSystem.lean, Modal/Basic.lean, Modal/Semantics/Birelational.lean docs, plus AxiomDiaDuality -> AxiomDiamondDuality.

Phases 4-8: notation de-duplication, ONE module per phase, smallest-first by build cost -- LTL (1 collision, 2746 lines) -> Temporal (1, 20310) -> Bimodal (2, 52462) -> Propositional (3, 42561) -> Modal (5, 83504). Each phase deletes the listed declaration, adds the _def bridge lemma(s), and gates on `lake build <Module>` before proceeding.
Phase 9: full CI gate -- lake build, checkInitImports, lake lint, lint-style, lake test, mk_all --module, shake.
zero_debt_assessment: No step requires sorry, an axiom, or a vacuous definition. Every change is a deletion, a rename, or an rfl bridge lemma. If a _def bridge lemma fails to close by rfl, that indicates the instance and constructor have drifted -- escalate as [BLOCKED] rather than working around it.
